'''Hyman Bass''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|h|aɪ|m|ən|_|b|æ|s}}; born October 5, 1932)<ref name=MacTutor>[http://www.gap-system.org/~history/Biographies/Bass.html Hyman Bass.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110607140254/http://www.gap-system.org/~history/Biographies/Bass.html |date=2011-06-07 }} [[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]]. Accessed January 31, 2010</ref> is an American [[mathematician]], known for work in [[algebra]] and in [[mathematics education]]. From 1959 to 1998 he was Professor in the Mathematics Department at [[Columbia University]]. He is currently the [[Samuel Eilenberg]] Distinguished University Professor of Mathematics and Professor of Mathematics Education at the [[University of Michigan]].

==Life==
Born to a [[Jewish]] family in [[Houston]], [[Texas]],<ref name=MacTutor /> he earned his B.A. in 1955 from [[Princeton University]] and his Ph.D. in 1959 from the [[University of Chicago]].  His thesis, titled ''Global dimensions of rings'', was written under the supervision of [[Irving Kaplansky]].

He has held visiting appointments at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]],<ref>[http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/frontpage?page=10 Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130106223426/http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/frontpage?page=10 |date=2013-01-06 }}</ref> [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] and [[École Normale Supérieure]] (Paris), [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (Bombay), [[University of Cambridge]], [[University of California, Berkeley]], [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]], [[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada|IMPA]] (Rio), [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]], [[Mittag-Leffler Institute]] (Stockholm), and the [[University of Utah]]. He was president of the [[American Mathematical Society]].

Bass formerly chaired the Mathematical Sciences Education Board (1992–2000) at the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]], and the Committee on Education of the American Mathematical Society. He was the President of [[International Commission on Mathematical Instruction|ICMI]] from 1999 to 2006.<ref>[http://www.mathunion.org/icmi/about-icmi/executive-committee/past-executive-committees/ ICMI Executive Committees 1908–2009.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927013928/http://www.mathunion.org/icmi/about-icmi/executive-committee/past-executive-committees/ |date=2011-09-27 }}  [[International Commission on Mathematical Instruction]]. Accessed January 31, 2010</ref>  Since 1996 he has been collaborating with [[Deborah Loewenberg Ball|Deborah Ball]] and her research group at the University of Michigan on the mathematical knowledge and resources entailed in the teaching of mathematics at the elementary level. He has worked to build bridges between diverse professional communities and stakeholders involved in [[mathematics education]].

==Work==
His research interests have been in [[algebraic K-theory]], [[commutative algebra]] and [[algebraic geometry]], [[algebraic group]]s, geometric methods in [[group theory]], and [[Ihara zeta function|ζ functions on finite simple graphs]].

==Awards and recognitions==
Bass was elected as a member of the National Academy of Sciences in 1982.<ref name=NAS>{{cite web|title=Bass, Hyman|url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/480321314?pg=vprof&mbr=1001664|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120117194523/http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/480321314?pg=vprof&mbr=1001664|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 17, 2012|work=National Academy of Sciences|access-date=May 20, 2011}}</ref> In 1983, he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780–2010: Chapter B|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterB.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=May 20, 2011}}</ref> In 2002 he was elected a fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20160818090620/http://twas.org/sites/default/files/member/hb_vita_2015_april.pdf Hyman Bass, CV, twas.org]</ref> He is a 2006 [[National Medal of Science]] laureate.<ref>[https://www.nsf.gov/news/news_summ.jsp?cntn_id=109741 President to Award 2005–2006 National Medals of Science and National Medals of Technology Honoring Nation's Leading Researchers, Inventors and Innovator.] [[National Science Foundation]]. Accessed January 31, 2010</ref> In 2009 he was elected a member of the National Academy of Education.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.soe.umich.edu/news_events/news/article/hyman_bass_elected_to_the_national_academy_of_education/ |title=Hyman Bass Elected to the National Academy of Education, U. of Michigan Department of Education |access-date=2015-10-07 |archive-date=2015-10-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151030213443/http://www.soe.umich.edu/news_events/news/article/hyman_bass_elected_to_the_national_academy_of_education/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref> He was awarded the [[Mary P. Dolciani Award]] in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dolciani Award {{!}} Mathematical Association of America|url=https://www.maa.org/node/310|access-date=2020-09-27|website=www.maa.org}}</ref>
